name: study
description: Learn a subject through sub-topics and flashcard quizzes. Good for exam prep, courses (math, science, languages), or interview preparation. Quiz any single sub-category or the whole subject.
setup_questions: What subject are you studying? (e.g., Calculus, Organic Chemistry, System Design interviews)
What sub-categories/topics does it cover? (comma-separated, e.g., Derivatives, Integrals, Limits — you can add more later with /pensare:study-add)

context_files.name: Overview.md
context_files.description: Study plan: subject summary, sub-category list with card counts, and a quiz-progress tracker

dynamic_directories.description: Split the answer to setup question 2 on commas. For each item, create one kebab-case directory containing the files below.

files.name: flashcards.md
files.template:
# Flashcards — {subcategory}

<!--
Add flashcards below. Format (leave one blank line between cards):

Q: your question here
A: the answer (may span multiple lines)

Helpers:
  /pensare:study-add {subcategory}    add or auto-generate cards
  /pensare:study-quiz {subcategory}   quiz yourself on this sub-category
-->

files.name: notes.md
files.template:
# Notes — {subcategory}

_Study notes for {subcategory}: summaries, formulas, worked examples, gotchas._

Tip: run `/pensare:study-add {subcategory}` and choose "generate from notes" to turn
these notes into flashcards.

structure.overview_template:
# {subject} — Study Plan

_Pensare study project: {project_name}_

## Subject

{project_description}

## Sub-Categories

Each sub-category is a folder with `flashcards.md` (the deck) and `notes.md`.

| Sub-Category | Cards | Last Quiz | Best Score |
|--------------|-------|-----------|------------|
{subject_table}

Add a new sub-category anytime: `/pensare:study-add <new-topic>`

## Progress

Quiz results land here (newest first). Start one with `/pensare:study-quiz`
(no argument = whole subject, or pass a sub-category name).

| Date | Scope | Score | Missed | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|--------|-------|

## Study Log

Use `/pensare note` to journal what you studied, weak areas, and goals.
